Only page.test.tsx changed after Cycle 1 (+253 lines). The temporary RED breaks were reverted with zero residue.

Test non-vacuity — VERIFIED: assertions read live rendered output and real dummy computation, not tautologies. Density asserts the actual <th> class (py-3/py-2/py-4) and localStorage; summary asserts the rendered data-testid='table-summary' text; sort/paging assert the captured fetch URL params; dummy parity asserts deep equality against an independent compareRows computation, the exact offset slice (ids of rows 3..6) and nextCursor=6, and a zero-network counter. 14/14 promotions tests pass; 260/260 full suite; `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

Reference-consistency — VERIFIED: the promotions implementation mirrors the approved T12 products page and T13 users page (same sortRef/cursorRef pattern, same shared helpers, same TableSummary/TablePagination/TableDensityToggle wiring).

strengths: The offset-cursor contract is implemented at a single derivation point (`nextCursor: cursor + limit`, api.ts:185) and the id-based `next_cursor` is never read or sent — the exact behavior the QUALITY BAR must-have/red-flag pair targets.

Dummy parity is achieved through the shared compareRows/paginate helpers rather than bespoke logic, covering created_at-DESC→id-DESC fallback, offset slice, total=filtered.length and the 4-state {total,active,scheduled,ended} breakdown, with a verified zero-network guarantee.

The 4-state dummy buckets are mutually exclusive by construction (active/scheduled/ended partition the list), so they always sum to total — the test pins this with a deep-equality assertion at a fake clock.

sortRef/cursorRef keep sort/cursor out of loadPromotions' dependency list, so header clicks and page changes do not re-trigger the mount effect and reset the page; the reset rules (sort → cursor=0, paging → preserve) are applied explicitly at each call site.

sortableColumns is the exact rendered-keys ∩ allowlist intersection including both created_at and updated_at and correctly excluding 'name' (absent from the promotions allowlist) and 'action' — no phantom sortable column that would silently fall back server-side.

The three commits stayed strictly within the 3 in-scope files; page.tsx/api.ts are byte-identical to Cycle 1 and the CRUD/broadcast functions are byte-identical to the pre-task baseline, so the promotion write/broadcast flow is provably preserved.

Tests exercise real rendered behavior (aria-sort attributes, em-dash cells, summary text, fetch-URL params, dummy ordering/slice) rather than tautologies, and the em-dash, offset-slice and invalid-sort edge cases are covered.

issues.description: The sort-defaulting idiom `const sortCol = filters.sort || 'created_at'; const sortOrder = filters.order === 'asc' ? 'asc' : 'desc';` is repeated across the dummy branches of outlets/products/users/promotions api.ts (4 occurrences on this plan), while the shared `normalizeSort` helper (lib/admin-table.ts:44) already encapsulates it. This is a pre-existing cross-page pattern inherited from the already-approved T4/T12/T13 dummy branches (none of which were flagged for it), and refactoring only promotions would make it inconsistent while refactoring all four would touch out-of-scope files — so it is recorded as a non-blocking observation rather than a defect introduced by T14.

page.tsx is 307 lines and the single AdminPromotionsPage component spans ~270 lines (page.tsx:38-307), marginally above the ~300-line soft threshold / 50-line function heuristic. The bulk is declarative JSX (the columns array + two Modal blocks) and the shape mirrors the approved products (239) and users (217) pages, so it is noted as a maintainability observation rather than a blocking split; the sibling pages were approved at similar sizes.

listDummyPromotions does not validate the requested sort against SORT_ALLOWLISTS.promotions, so an out-of-allowlist column (e.g. 'bogus') resolves to an all-null comparison and falls back to id-DESC rather than the backend's documented created_at-DESC fallback. The UI only ever emits allowlisted columns via sortableColumns, and the test confirms the behavior is deterministic and non-throwing, so the divergence is unreachable in practice — the same non-allowlisted dummy behavior exists in the approved users/products/outlets branches.
